what_slowed_me_down: The context.dev /web/scrape/markdown endpoint worked reliably for all 40 pricing pages (only one redirect, Semrush, which still landed on a valid pricing page), so throughput was good overall. The main slowdowns: (1) The monid CLI is not preinstalled and the global npm install failed with EACCES, requiring a sudo fallback before setup could begin. (2) Each scrape runs synchronously with --wait and there is no documented batch/parallel mode for the CLI, so 40 pages had to be fetched sequentially at ~5-10s each; a background shell loop was needed to keep the session responsive, and the first background attempt was killed when the shell timed out. (3) The scraper captures whatever billing toggle state the page defaults to (monthly vs annual), which varies per site, so each markdown still had to be read by hand to decide whether to divide yearly prices by 12 - the markdown is clean but plan/price extraction is not structured. (4) A few pages render prices in fragments (e.g. Clockify's 'US$ 5 .49', Jotform's '$**39**'), which required regex archaeology in the markdown. Cost was very reasonable: about $13 for 40 pages.
